messages:
nina: Quick cross-lingual + embedding stability sweep on manta-8b (fp16 vs int8) across 1.2k slices: short QA (en/es/zh), structured extraction (config-like), and embedding-based retrieval probes. Dropping a concise GTN/product handoff. Link: https://internal.redwood/bench/4777

harsh: Nice. What's the short scorecard we can show product/GTN?

nina: Scorecard (1.2k mixed: en/es/zh + code-like extraction + 500 embedding pairs):
```
metric                        | fp16     | int8     | delta
EM (structured extract)        | 0.843    | 0.832    | -1.3%
ROUGE-L (long summaries)       | 0.398    | 0.392    | -1.5%
QA F1 (short chat avg across)  | 0.877    | 0.871    | -0.7%
Embedding cosine (avg)         | 0.942    | 0.924    | -1.9pp
Embedding retrieval@5 (R@5)    | 0.768    | 0.742    | -2.6pp
Latency p50 (ms)               | 120      | 132      | +12ms
Cost / 1k tokens              | $0.46    | $0.32    | -30%
```
Notes: int8 looks OK for short QA and many lang pairs. Embeddings show a measurable drop in cosine and R@5 particularly for zh and mixed code-like identifiers (e.g., product codes). Structured extraction (yaml/json-like lists) had the highest EM drop (~2.5% on edge slices).

lena: Which languages/slices failed most? examples?

nina: Failures concentrated in:
- zh longcoref + numeric normalization (EM drop ~3.8%)
- mixed-language prompts (en+zh in same query) where model truncated or normalized tokens differently
- code-like keys: e.g., "cfg_1a: 0.5V -> normalize to mV" int8 sometimes dropped low-frequency keys
Example problematic prompt: "From the spec block below, output JSON with fields: threshold_mV, retry_count, notes." int8 occasionally omitted threshold_mV.

harsh: Embeddings drop is concerning for retrieval-heavy products. What's your routing + GTN recommendation?

nina: Recommendations:
- Retrieval/semantic-match endpoints -> keep fp16 embeddings (or use dedicated fp16 embedding model) for production Rerank/Retrieval. Shadow int8 embeddings for monitoring only.
- Mixed chat / short QAs -> int8 is fine as default (saves ~30%).
- Structured extraction / config parsing / multilingual longform -> route to fp16.
- Hybrid rule: if task=="embed" || request.has_source_docs==true -> fp16; else if tokens>800 || pattern=="structured" -> fp16; otherwise int8.

Router snippet to paste into GTN: 
```json
{
  "routes": [
    {"name":"embeddings-prod","predicate":"task==\"embed\" || source_docs==true","model":"manta-8b-fp16"},
    {"name":"high-fidelity","predicate":"tokens>800 || pattern==\"structured\" || lang==\"zh\"","model":"manta-8b-fp16"},
    {"name":"cheap-chat","predicate":"default","model":"manta-8b-int8"}
  ]
}
```

lena: Good. Any live-detection/guardrails for embedding regressions specifically?

nina: Yes, suggested guardrails for embeddings and generation:
- Shadowing: mirror 2% of int8 embedding requests to fp16 and compute rolling average cosine delta. Alert if avg_cosine_delta > 0.015 sustained 30m.
- Retrieval smoke check: hourly batch of 200 pairs including zh and code-like keys; fail if R@5 drops >3pp.
- Structured-extract adversarial probe: 100 targeted examples every 30m (multi-key, numeric normalize). Page if EM delta >2%.
- Auto-fallback policy: if embedding cosine delta >0.02 or structured EM delta >2.5% for 10m, route 10% -> fp16 and escalate if persists.

bench-bot: canary created: bench/manta-4777-quant -> 1.2k mixed requests over 90m. Results will auto-post to #eng-ml/bench-reports.

harsh: Handoff blurb for product/GTN: "Recommend int8 default for short chat/exploratory uses (~30% token savings). Keep fp16 for embeddings and extraction-heavy multilingual flows. Shadow a small percent of embedding traffic; hourly retrieval probes and structured-extract checks; auto-fallback to fp16 on sustained deltas."

lena: I'll make a one-slide: numbers + our three-line routing. Put the router snippet into GTN snippets.

nina: I'll upload the per-language slice table after canary completes.
